---
title: TUI
---

## Overview

The SearcherKit terminal UI (TUI) is an interactive front end for running ad hoc
SearcherKit queries. It streams model reasoning, assistant output, and tool activity
as the agent works, while writing the same history and trace information used by the
runtime to disk.

Each submitted query starts a fresh, independent agent run. The TUI keeps a visible
session history for convenience, but earlier questions and answers are not added to
the next query's model context.

## Usage

Start the TUI with the packaged default configuration:

```bash
searcherkit tui
```

To use a recipe or another Hydra configuration, pass its directory and config name:

```bash
searcherkit tui \
  --config-path websailor \
  --config-name websailor
```

Hydra-style overrides may follow the command options:

```bash
searcherkit tui \
  --config-path websailor \
  --config-name websailor \
  agent.llm_client.model=Qwen3-8B
```

Type a question at the `>` prompt and press **Enter**. The interface shows the active
model, active source, and record directory in the status bar. Model output is
streamed into the current turn, and search or visit calls appear as tool interaction
blocks.

::: {.callout-note}
The TUI uses the configured agent, parser, sources, and tools. Validate a recipe with
`searcherkit inspect` before opening the TUI when you are creating or changing its
configuration.
:::

## Commands and keyboard controls

Type `/` to open the command menu. Use the arrow keys to highlight an entry, **Tab**
to complete it, and **Enter** to run it.

| Command | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `/models` | Open the available-model submenu, when model discovery succeeded |
| `/sources` | Open the configured-source submenu |
| `/thinking` | Show or hide assistant reasoning blocks |
| `/tool-detail` | Switch tool interactions between preview and full detail |
| `/clear` | Clear the live transcript while keeping the TUI open |
| `/quit` | Exit the TUI |

Selecting a model or source affects subsequent queries only. Selecting a source
rebinds built-in `search` and `visit` tools to that source for the next independent
run. The status bar always shows the effective selection.

The main keyboard controls are:

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **Enter** | Submit the current query or selected command |
| **Ctrl+J** | Insert a newline in the input field |
| **Up / Down** | Move through the command menu or query history |
| **Page Up / Page Down** | Scroll the transcript |
| **Escape** | Dismiss the command menu |
| **Ctrl+C** | Copy selected text, cancel a running query, clear input, or exit when idle |

Mouse scrolling moves through the transcript. Dragging across transcript text selects
and copies it to the system clipboard when clipboard integration is available.

Commands that change session state, clear the view, or quit are rejected while a
query is running. Press **Ctrl+C** to cancel the query first. A cancelled run is still
written as a record with `status: cancelled`.

## Interactive run records

Every query creates a JSON record plus trace logging. The default directory is
`outputs/interactive`, or `<output_path>/interactive` when the composed configuration
sets `output_path`. Choose another directory with `--interactive-output-path`:

```bash
searcherkit tui \
  --config-path recipe/websailor \
  --config-name websailor \
  --interactive-output-path outputs/tui-sessions
```

The directory contains timestamped run records, a global log, and per-query traces:

```text
outputs/interactive/
├── 20260715_143000_<trace-id>.json
├── run.log
└── traces/
    └── <trace-id>.log
```

Each record includes the input, status, event stream, serialized message history,
timing, and run statistics. Failed and cancelled queries are persisted as well, with
their error information, so interactive debugging does not lose the execution
context.
